title: Quadratic graphs
examples: How do I find the turning point from the equation?
What does the graph crossing the x-axis tell me?
Does the symmetry always go through the y-axis?

explain.say: Today we are looking at quadratic graphs. These graphs always make a U shape. This shape is called a parabola. Can you see the U shape on the screen?
The roots are where the graph crosses the x-axis. These are the values of x when y equals zero. For example, if the roots are two and five, the graph crosses at (2, 0) and (5, 0).
The turning point is the very bottom or the very top of the U shape. It is the minimum or maximum point. This point is important for knowing the graph's lowest or highest value.

draw.text: Turning Point: Lowest or highest point

explain.say: The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the vertical y-axis. To find this, you simply set x to zero in the equation. For example, if x is zero, you find the y value.
Symmetry means the graph is a mirror image. For a parabola, the line passing through the turning point is the line of symmetry. The graph is the same on both sides of this line.

draw.text: Symmetry: Mirror image across a line

faq.q: What are the roots of a quadratic graph?
faq.a: The roots are the points where the graph crosses the horizontal x-axis. At these points, the value of y must be zero. You might also hear this called the x-intercepts.
asks: Where does the graph hit the x-axis?

faq.q: How do I find the turning point?
faq.a: You can find the turning point using the formula for the x-coordinate. This formula helps you locate the exact middle of the U shape. It is often found using the formula negative b over two a.
asks: What is the vertex of the parabola?
How do I find the minimum or maximum point?

faq.a: The y-intercept is the point where the graph crosses the vertical y-axis. To find it, you always substitute zero for x in the equation. This gives you the y value at that point.
asks: Where does the graph cross the y-axis?
What is the value when x is zero?

faq.q: Does the line of symmetry always pass through the y-axis?
faq.a: No, the line of symmetry passes through the turning point. It is a vertical line that divides the graph into two matching halves. It only passes through the y-axis if the turning point is on the y-axis.
asks: Is the line of symmetry always x equals zero?
Does the axis of symmetry always pass through the origin?

faq.q: What does the shape of the graph tell me?
faq.a: The shape tells you that the function is quadratic. It means the highest power of x in your equation is two. This U shape is what defines a parabola.
asks: What is the general shape of a quadratic graph?
What kind of curve is this?

facts: A quadratic graph is always in the shape of a parabola.
The roots are the points where the graph intersects the x-axis.
The turning point is the vertex of the parabola.
The line of symmetry is a vertical line passing through the turning point.

quiz.say: If a graph has roots at x equals negative two and x equals four, what is its line of symmetry?
quiz.why: The line of symmetry is exactly halfway between the two roots, which is one.

wrong.0: This assumes the symmetry is always on the y-axis, which is not always true.
wrong.2: This is the sum of the roots, but the symmetry is the average, not the total.
wrong.3: This is just the first root, but the symmetry must balance both points.

quiz.say: For the equation y equals x squared plus three, what is the y-intercept?
quiz.why: To find the y-intercept, you must set x to zero, making y equal to three.

wrong.0: This assumes the graph always passes through the origin, which is not guaranteed.
wrong.1: This is just an arbitrary point on the graph, not the specific intercept asked for.
wrong.3: This incorrectly swaps the x and y coordinates, confusing the intercept.

quiz.say: If the turning point of a graph is at (2, -5), what is the equation of its line of symmetry?
quiz.why: The line of symmetry must always be a vertical line passing directly through the x-coordinate of the turning point.

wrong.0: This uses the y-coordinate of the turning point as the x-value, which is incorrect.
wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes the turning point must lie on the y-axis.
wrong.3: This describes a horizontal line, but the axis of symmetry for a parabola is always vertical.
